trigger: CHECK(bodyEvent.hasException()) at HTTPDownstreamCoroSessionTests.cpp:1685 fails because HTTPStreamSource::readBodyEvent on the keepalive POST stream returns a SUSPEND value (no error_, empty bodyQueue_, canSuspend_ initially true) instead of an HTTPError.
originating_invariant: The test assumes the 1001 GET+RST_STREAM pairs are delivered to the RSTS RateLimitFilter (limit 1000 per 100ms), so the limit is breached, onError -> connectionError -> resetOpenStreams aborts the keepalive stream with CANCEL before the check runs. In FAIL that breach never happens: the session had already drained (GOAWAY last-stream=1) before the burst, so HTTP2Codec suppresses every callback for streams 3..2003 and the limiter never counts a single reset.

hypotheses.claim: loopN(4) uses blocking EventBase::loopOnce(). The POST dispatch finishes within the first two iterations, so the last two iterations sit idle and block until the next HHWheelTimer deadline. Under the FAIL schedule the fourth iteration blocks about 900ms until the fixture's 1s connection read timeout fires. The TestCoroTransport read returns TIMED_OUT, readLoop calls initiateDrain(), and HTTP2Codec::generateGoaway (sessionClosing_ OPEN, isWaitingToDrain true) sends GOAWAY with lastStream=1. deliverCallbackIfAllowed then suppresses onMessageBegin and onAbort for every burst stream (id > egressGoawayAck_=1), so the RSTS RateLimitFilter never counts them. Nothing breaches, the keepalive stream is never aborted, and readBodyEvent returns SUSPEND.

PASS seed 1 loopN(4) timeouts are -1, 0, 8ms, 100ms (about 110ms total), which never reaches the 1s timers. The gap from loopN(2) iteration 1 to evb_.loop() is 97.7ms in PASS (1001 handler coroutines dispatched) and 0.2ms in FAIL (no streams created), consistent with the codec suppressing the burst streams. The F line (21:01:54.726606) matches the evb_.loop() epoll_wait at 514.726. Code: readLoop TIMED_OUT -> initiateDrain (HTTPCoroSession.cpp:2601-2604); HTTP2Codec.cpp:1357-1377 sets lastStream=getLastIncomingStreamID() when OPEN; HTTPParallelCodec.h:89-127 deliverCallbackIfAllowed suppresses callbacks above egressGoawayAck_; parseRstStream delivers onAbort only through deliverCallbackIfAllowed; coro never enables double-GOAWAY drain. hypotheses.claim: The RSTS fixed 100ms window resets during the burst (timeoutExpired zeroes the counter), splitting the 1001 resets across two windows so neither exceeds 1000.
hypotheses.supporting: 1001 is exactly one over the limit, so there is no slack. Burst processing in loopN(2) iteration 0 takes about 440ms of virtual time, far more than 100ms.
hypotheses.contradicting: HTTPUniplexTransportSession::readLoop drains all 2002 queued events in one resumption: TestCoroTransport::read never suspends while events are queued, and readLoop only reschedules when a read returns >= 64000 bytes. HHWheelTimer callbacks cannot run in the middle of that synchronous callback. The same 440ms of processing happens in PASS and still breaches. In FAIL, no handler dispatch iteration follows, meaning streams were never created, which this hypothesis cannot explain.
hypotheses.next_experiment: Pre-fix, pin session_->setRateLimitParams(RateLimiter::Type::RSTS, 1000, 1h) in a scratch build and replay seed 0. H2 predicts PASS; H1 predicts FAIL is unchanged.

hypotheses.claim: Ordering race: the verification coroutine (posted through evb_.add / notification queue, which runs in the libevent phase ahead of loop callbacks) runs before the readLoop has processed the burst, because loopN(2) is not enough iterations.
hypotheses.supporting: Notification-queue work runs before runInLoop callbacks within an iteration, and the check starts in the first evb_.loop() iteration.
hypotheses.contradicting: Loop-iteration counts do not depend on the schedule, and PASS uses the same loopN(2). In both runs loopN(2) iteration 0 is non-blocking and carries about 440ms of burst-processing work, so the readLoop resumed and consumed the burst before the check was even posted.
